decisions.claim: ssh can authenticate with a default identity file instead of the broker key
decisions.reason: confirmed, and I had IdentitiesOnly backwards — it restricts AGENT-offered identities to configured ones, it does not stop ssh using ~/.ssh/id_*. Fix: write the PUBLIC key (not secret) into the 0700 dir and pass -o IdentityFile=<pub> with IdentitiesOnly=yes, the documented way to pin one agent identity.

decisions.claim: remote_argv is joined and re-interpreted by the remote shell
decisions.reason: confirmed. `ssh host -- a b c` concatenates into ONE string for the remote shell, so a `;` in an argument executes. Local argv safety was never remote argv safety. Each element is now shell-quoted for the remote side.

decisions.claim: the tool API does not match the spec's vault_ssh_exec(entry_id, host, argv[], purpose)
decisions.reason: the spec is stale, not the code. That exact signature IS round 1's F2 bug — an argv carrying its own destination alongside an advisory host field. Changing the API was the fix. Updating SPEC.md to match rather than reintroducing the vulnerability.

decisions.claim: a bogus frame length stalls the connection forever
decisions.reason: the length is authoritative so a client declaring 32 and sending 1 is malformed, but hanging on it is still wrong. Added a per-connection idle timeout so a stalled peer is dropped rather than held open.

decisions.claim: rsync audit records the destination, not the host actually connected to
decisions.reason: confirmed. With two allowlisted hosts, rsync can target the second while every signature line names the first. The audited host now comes from the rsync arguments themselves.
